title: flake: a call in a chat of more than two was created, not refused
description:
Seen once in a full `cargo test --workspace --all-features` run on
2026-11-26, in crates/mimid-agent/tests/vtc.rs:685
(a_call_in_a_chat_of_more_than_two_is_refused). Passes 3 of 3 alone and
2 of 2 as a whole test file, so it only shows under the parallel
workspace run.

## What happened

The test pushes carol and dave into the chat's `participants`, so a call
would hold three, then creates a VTCCall and expects `notCreated` with
`invalidProperties`. The run got a created call instead:
`"created":{"k":{...,"activeParticipantCount":1,...}}` and
`"notCreated":null`.

So the serving path saw a chat with two participants or fewer at the
moment it checked.

## The two readings, neither ruled out

1. Test: the mutation through `alice.store.state()` is not durably
   visible to the serving path by the time the POST is handled, and the
   test only usually wins that race.
2. Product: the VTC create path reads a participant list captured
   earlier -- a snapshot or a cache -- rather than the current one, and
   under load the stale copy is what it checks.

Reading 2 is why this is P1 rather than a test annoyance. The assertion
is a policy refusal: a call in a group chat being allowed because the
participant count read low is a real defect, and the same stale read
would affect any other check over `participants`.

## Next step

Find what the create path reads `participants` from and whether it can
be older than the last committed write. If it reads through the same
store handle the test writes to, the race is the test's and the fix is
to make the write observable before the POST. If it reads a cached
snapshot, the bead is a product bug and needs a regression test that
fails before the fix.

Do not "fix" this by raising a timeout or retrying the assertion: both
readings would stay.

Related: bead mimid-gn1w is a different flake in the same full-workspace
runs (an SSE subscribe that does not establish). Same trigger --
parallel load -- different mechanism.
